result:
I added Japanese as a second language with a switcher in the site header. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (8 tests, including 6 new ones) and the project's catalog check (`guren check --i18n`) all pass. I didn't boot the app or try the switcher in a real browser.

- **Switching language:** `POST /locale` takes `{ locale }` (`en` or `ja`), is open to guests and signed-in users, and saves the pick in a `locale` cookie for one year. It then redirects to the `Referer`, or to `/` when there isn't one. Any other value, or a missing field, goes through the same route validation that rejects a bad post title, so it fails the same way and the cookie isn't touched.
- **First visits and later ones:** the framework reads the cookie before `Accept-Language`, so a saved pick beats the browser's setting. With no pick, a browser asking for Japanese gets Japanese; otherwise pages stay English. Pages report this in `_i18n.locale`.
- **Referer from another site:** the redirect keeps only its path, so the switcher can't be used to send people off-site. That's a small addition beyond the request.
- **Catalogs:** the text lives in `lang/en/` and `lang/ja/` as `nav.json`, `posts.json` and `auth.json`, plus a Japanese `messages.json` holding the existing welcome message. Both languages have the same 30 keys, including the nine from the table.
- **Header links:** the brand name already linked to `/`, so the new `nav.home` link to `/` is a second one.
- **Japanese text:** I wrote the translations myself. 新規投稿 is the header link to write a post and also the New page heading. Someone fluent should review the rest before launch.

`src/app.ts` now lists `['en', 'ja']` as supported languages. I added `LocalePayloadSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts` and `LocaleController` in `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts`, and registered `POST /locale` in `routes/web.ts`. `Layout.tsx` gets a `select` language switcher, with its labels taken from the catalogs, and every header label now comes from the catalogs. `posts/Index`, `Show`, `New` and `Edit` read all their labels through `useTranslation()`, so no page contains 「記事」 itself. I reran codegen to update the files in `.guren/`, and the new tests are in `tests/LocaleController.test.ts`.
